question: The curve that shows the levels of output that a profit maximising firm would choose a produce at different values of the market price is called the firm's _________.
solution:
The correct answer is__** supply curve.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The supply Curve shows the levels of output that a profit-maximizing firm would choose a product at different values of the market price.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e01a13f2d7237487a1f3af13af608fb12158aac94827d9b4066bc8b2211ceb3.png] **

 
• The supply curve is** upward sloping because, over time, suppliers can choose how much of their goods to produce and later bring to market.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Demand Curve**

 
 
• **​a graphic representation of the relationship between product price and the quantity of the product demanded.**​
 
 
 
• **Performance Curve**
 
 
• also known as a** bell curve, is a systematic measure for assessing employees' performance via a graphic diagram.**
 
 
 
• **Variable Curve**
 
 
• **A curve that graphically represents the relation between the total variable cost incurred by a firm in the short-run production of a good or service and the quantity produced.​**
 
 

ca:T
